files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller checklist

Prepared by L. Mbeki. Complete in sequence; no shortcuts.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July; some months all runs pay in-month. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule, contracts, and GL. If it is not already posted, book June prepaid amortization as ONE combined journal entry; do not duplicate an existing entry. Take a full month of amortization in the month an item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after verifying the GL to prevent a duplicate posting.
5. Check June vendor-bill documents against the GL, verify expense coding, and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, after obligations 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Wildwood Supply Co. began in 2018 when two former outdoor-retail coworkers noticed that customers wanted practical, attractive household and workday goods without having to sort through endless online listings. They started with a tightly edited assortment packed from a borrowed stockroom, writing product notes in the plainspoken style they wished more shops used.

Today, the company is an ecommerce merchant selling desk accessories, storage pieces, reusable travel gear, packing essentials, and small tools for home and field. The catalog favors durable materials, uncomplicated designs, and products that can earn their shelf space. Orders move through a mix of direct vendor relationships and a compact fulfillment operation.

The team has a hands-on character. Merchandising swaps customer stories with support, operations keeps a running list of packaging improvements, and marketing is known for testing cheerful campaign ideas before turning them into polished launches. Finance is small, practical, and closely involved with purchasing and inventory.

Wildwood Supply Co. is currently refining its assortment, improving repeat-customer communications, and tightening the handoff between campaign planning and fulfillment. The business remains focused on dependable service, sensible growth, and keeping its distinctive editorial voice as its customer base develops.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Give Wildwood Supply Co. a warmer, more recognizable look without losing the practical tone customers already know. The refresh should emphasize useful goods, honest product guidance, and the people who pack and support each order.

## Priorities

- Roll out the brand refresh across the storefront, email templates, packaging inserts, and core social profiles.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter, built around organization, everyday carry, and practical care tips rather than hard-sell product demos.
- Pilot a partner co-marketing program with a complementary maker or small business. Start with shared editorial content, then test a coordinated campaign if the audience fit is strong.
- Improve repeat-purchase messaging through post-purchase education, replenishment reminders, and curated follow-up recommendations.
- Build a reusable library of customer photos, short product demonstrations, and behind-the-scenes fulfillment stories.

## Quarter focus

**Q3:** Complete creative direction, refresh priority channels, recruit webinar guests, and select a pilot partner.

**Q4:** Expand the strongest refreshed campaigns, run the partner pilot, and package webinar material into evergreen email and social content.

## Measurement

Track qualified traffic, email engagement, repeat ordering, webinar participation, and partner-sourced visits. Review results by channel and document which messages should carry into the next planning cycle. Budget remains pending the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Handoff notes from your chatty predecessor

L. Mbeki — a few things I learned the fussy way:

- The bank slips its own fees and charges in near the end of the statement. We normally book those during close, not as they occur during the month, so do not assume they are already in the ledger.
- Give the June vendor bills a careful coding review. A couple may be sitting in the wrong expense accounts, and the documents in `bills/` are authoritative if the GL description tells a different story.
- The budget was fixed early, at the start of the quarter. The one-off June items were never planned, and they are usually the explanation for the big budget-to-actual variances.
- Payroll timing is a little different this month: the second June run pays in early July. Check the register before booking the accrual.
